subject.title: Feature Request: Voice Recognition / Speaker Identification for Voice Interface

question: Should OpenClaw add enrolled-speaker gating to native and realtime voice, and where should enrollment state, provider egress, thresholds, fallback behavior, and plugin/API ownership live?
rationale: The report is valid but the next step changes sensitive voice state, probabilistic command gating, config/storage shape, and native/provider boundaries, which automation cannot choose safely.

options.title: Design the cross-platform speaker gate first
options.body: Specify the enrollment, storage, fallback, provider, and security contract before accepting implementation work across macOS, iOS, Android, gateway, and config surfaces.

options.title: Route this to plugin/API design
options.body: Keep core voice behavior unchanged until a plugin or SDK capability can own speaker verification without adding optional policy to core.

options.title: Defer until voice matures further
options.body: Leave current wake-word/PTT/Talk behavior as-is and revisit speaker recognition after the voice-and-realtime-talk surface is more stable.

recommendation.title: Design the cross-platform speaker gate first
recommendation.body: Specify the enrollment, storage, fallback, provider, and security contract before accepting implementation work across macOS, iOS, Android, gateway, and config surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main voice carry-forward plus broad touched-surface context makes this the best available routing candidate, although ownership is shared across native and config areas.
